doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

chapter: Tuba in jazz history and technique
title: 'Tunk', 'Bemsha Swing' from Don Cherry, and 'CJ'
summary: 'Tunk' uses the 'Bemsha Swing' bass line taught by Don Cherry; his one non-bass-line composition is 'CJ' for his son.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Thank you. This particular tune is entitled “Tunk,” T-U-N-K. And the T-U is for the tuba and the N-K is for Monk because the bass line for this tune comes from Monk’s composition “Bemsha Swing.”

It was taught to me by Don Cherry when I worked with Don Cherry. He taught me “Bemsha Swing” and this was the bass line [scats]. You know so this bass line comes from “Bemsha Swing” and what I did was just superimpose another melody on the top of it because it’s a great bass line for the tuba. A lot of my things that I choose to do are bass

line kind of driven. The only one composition I’ve written that wasn’t and that was a song for my son called “CJ” and it just — the melody came to me while watching him move around the house, where he — it’s in seven and then it switches back to six. So I mean you see him walking and he’s like —
Is this the son that’s going to Eastman?
That’s the one that’s going to Eastman. He’ll be like 20 years old — month after next.
